partner_context.their_ambition: D-Marin operates one of the Mediterranean's largest premium marina networks — berths and waterfront destinations across Croatia, Greece, Turkey, Montenegro, Italy, Spain and the UAE — and is positioning its marinas as connected lifestyle destinations, not just parking for boats.
partner_context.their_pressure: Marina guests still arrive by road and leave their berth by tender or charter; there is no clean, fast, branded way to move people between a D-Marin marina and the islands, resorts and airports around it. As marinas decarbonize and compete on experience, the missing piece is mobility between the dots they already own.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: D-Marin's marinas are the perfect berthing-and-charging backbone for a foiling-electric network. Navier turns a network of premium marinas into a network of premium mobility nodes — fast silent low-wake transfers between marinas, islands, resorts and airports, all charging at berths D-Marin already operates.

hero.title: Navier × D-Marin — marinas that move people
hero.subtitle: Turning a pan-Mediterranean marina network into a foiling-electric mobility network.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet; D-Marin brings the berths, the charging backbone and the waterfront destinations across the Mediterranean. Together we connect the marinas D-Marin already owns into a clean, fast, branded mobility layer — marina-to-island, marina-to-airport and marina-to-marina — anchored on the live Maldives proof case.

why_now: D-Marin's marinas span exactly the Mediterranean clusters where Navier's island and coastal cases are sharpest — the Croatian islands, the Saronic and Cyclades, the Turkish coast, Montenegro's Boka Bay. Marinas already have the one thing electric mobility needs that destinations lack: shore power at every berth. The network and the charging are already built; the missing layer is the vessel.
multimodal_fit: A D-Marin marina becomes the hub: guests arrive by road or air, step onto a foiling transfer to the islands or the next marina, and the legacy tender/charter fleet keeps only the longest or most bespoke legs. Each marina is both a charging node and a demand node.

journeys_unlocked.today: Scheduled catamaran — sells out in summer.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: Premium foiling link along southern Dalmatia.

differentiation.why_navier: The only foiling-electric platform that turns a marina network into a mobility network — charging at berths D-Marin already operates, low-wake to protect marina basins and anchorages, near-silent, and proven at fleet scale in the Maldives.

objections.response: D-Marin doesn't have to operate them directly — it provides the berthing-and-charging backbone and the branded destination network; the foiling layer drives berth demand, draws guests between marinas and differentiates the network. Operating models flex from licensing to JV.
objections.concern: Why would a marina operator run vessels?

objections.response: The foil flies above the chop for a smoother ride. Pioneer II covers the marina-to-island and marina-to-marina legs all-electric; Quanta-LR hybrid carries the longer inter-cluster runs with no charging dependence.
Yes — every D-Marin berth has shore power; Pioneer II charges at a berth pedestal between runs. The network's existing infrastructure is the enabling asset.
objections.concern: Is the charging real across the network?

objections.response: Croatia (Mandalika/Šibenik–Split–Kornati) or Greece (Saronic) — the densest island-transfer demand against D-Marin's strongest berth positions — then replicate marina-by-marina across the network.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Croatia island cluster
phases.narrative: Launch from the D-Marin Croatian marinas (Mandalina/Šibenik, Borik) into the Split–Kornati–island corridors — the densest premium island-transfer demand against D-Marin's strongest berths.
phases.rationale: Prove the marina-as-mobility-node model where island-transfer demand and berth strength align.

phases.narrative: Extend to the Greek (Zea, Gouvia) and Turkish (Didim, Turgutreis) marinas — Saronic, Cyclades and Bodrum-coast transfers between D-Marin berths and the islands.
phases.rationale: Replicate across the eastern-Med marinas where demand and berths align.

phases.label: Phase 3 — pan-network mobility layer
phases.narrative: A foiling-electric mobility layer across the D-Marin network — Croatia, Greece, Turkey, Montenegro and the UAE — marinas connected as charging-and-demand nodes.
phases.rationale: Complete the network-wide layer, including the UAE marinas as a Gulf anchor.

the_ask.partner_brings: The pan-Mediterranean berth-and-charging backbone, the branded waterfront destinations and the marina-by-marina rollout sequence.

close.title: The berths and the charging are already built.
close.body: D-Marin already owns the hardest part of electric marine mobility — a network of premium berths with shore power across the Mediterranean. Navier adds the one missing layer: the vessel that connects them.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

steady_state.tam_framing: A premium marina network spanning seven countries, each berth a charging-and-demand node.

end_state.narrative: Steady state turns a network of premium marinas into a network of premium mobility nodes across the Mediterranean and the Gulf.
